8.1: Arjuna asks seven questions: what is Brahman, the Self, action, the material principle, the divine principle?
8.2: And who is the principle of sacrifice in this body, and how are you known at the time of death by the self-controlled?
8.3: Brahman is the imperishable Supreme; its own nature is called the Self; the creative force is called action.
8.4: The perishable is the material principle, the Person is the divine principle, and I Myself am the sacrifice in the body.
8.5: Whoever remembers Me alone while leaving the body at death attains My being — there is no doubt of this.
8.6: Whatever state one remembers at the end, that state one attains, being ever absorbed in its thought.
8.7: Therefore remember Me at all times and fight; with mind and intellect fixed on Me you will surely come to Me.
8.8: With mind engaged in constant practice and not straying elsewhere, one reaches the supreme Person.
8.9: Meditating on the ancient Seer, the ruler, subtler than the atom, sustainer of all, beyond darkness —
8.10: — at the time of death, with a steady mind, devotion, and the breath drawn between the brows, one reaches Him.
8.11: That state the knowers of the Veda call imperishable, which the desireless enter, and for which seekers practise continence.
8.12: Closing all the gates, confining the mind in the heart, fixing the breath in the head, established in concentration —
8.13: — uttering Om, the single syllable of Brahman, and remembering Me, one departs and attains the highest goal.
8.14: For one who remembers Me constantly with an undistracted mind, I am easy to reach — the ever-steadfast yogi.
8.15: Having come to Me, these great souls do not take rebirth in this impermanent house of sorrow.
8.16: All worlds up to Brahma's world are subject to return; but after reaching Me there is no rebirth.
8.17: Those who know Brahma's day and night — a thousand ages each — truly know day and night.
8.18: At the coming of day all manifest beings issue from the unmanifest; at night they dissolve back into it.
8.19: The same multitude of beings is born again and again, dissolving helplessly at nightfall and issuing at daybreak.
8.20: Beyond that unmanifest there is another unmanifest, eternal, which does not perish when all beings perish.
8.21: That imperishable unmanifest is called the highest goal; reaching it, one does not return — that is My supreme abode.
8.22: That supreme Person is attainable by undivided devotion, within whom all beings dwell and by whom all this is pervaded.
8.23: Now the times at which yogis depart, to return or not to return.
8.24: Fire, light, day, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern course — those who go then reach Brahman.
8.25: Smoke, night, the dark fortnight, the six months of the southern course — the yogi attains the lunar light and returns.
8.26: These two paths, light and dark, are eternal; by one there is no return, by the other one returns again.
8.27: No yogi who knows these two paths is ever deluded; therefore be steadfast in yoga at all times.
8.28: Knowing all this, the yogi transcends the fruits of study, sacrifice, austerity and charity, and attains the supreme primal state.
